established: Explicit initializeFresh only with both journal and marker absent; normal reads/mutations never reset storage. Existing and half-created unmarked stores reject without automatic import.
Each marker binds absolute kind/path/binding identity and random initialization generation. Retained shared state pins both peer generations and exact original paths/ceiling.
Bounded stable file reads reject symlink/hardlink/exposed storage and ambiguous or oversized JSON; Linux directory fsync errors propagate. Windows ACLs remain operator responsibility.

Writer locks are exclusive and exact-inode/token checked after asynchronous mutation and before rename. Original rows survive failed in-memory mutation, replacement and ambiguous directory durability.
Changed or unreadable shared callback outcomes retain the shared lock and original financial hold. Known unchanged local validation refusals permit retry.

Actual local filesystem tests delete each ledger/marker, reinitialize whole peer pairs against retained shared state, corrupt records, race writers and replace lock/data inodes. Existing supplier planning/closure/signed-binding/reserve cohorts remain green.
Original version-1 financial record schemas, IDs, 128-record bounds and canceled-unsubmitted reserve release semantics remain unchanged.
limits: Local storage is not rollback-proof. Deleting or rolling back all journals/markers/shared anchors together cannot be detected locally and requires independently reviewed external inventory/accounting.
No legacy migration/import or automatic stale-lock recovery was implemented. Stop all writers and reconcile original pending external identities/liabilities before operator recovery.
read() remains independent diagnostic file state and does not resolve a held lock or establish final external settlement.
This local fixture/filesystem cohort is not live Akash/Nosana execution, production custody acceptance or whole-backend/Linux regression. No new M6 execution completion credit is claimed.
